PHOTOS Halloween returns to Itaewon Listen Listen Text Size Print Summary Close summary Itaewon, Seoul, saw Halloween crowds return on Saturday, with the main road closed to traffic and tens of thousands of pedestrians celebrating. The neighborhood had spent the years after the 2022 crowd crush under cautious commemoration and heavy police presence. More people wore costumes, and parents with young children visited early. Line 6 trains began skipping Itaewon Station at 11:47 p.m., followed by an emergency alert about overcrowding on World Culture Food Street at 11:50 p.m.
How many years does it take a neighborhood to recover from tragedy? Four years ago, central Seoul's multicultural Itaewon neighborhood suffered an unspeakable accident, when over 150 people were crushed to death in a crowded alley.
In the two years following the disaster, there was an atmosphere of cautious commemoration under the watchful eye of a heavy police presence, as people worked through their trauma — and also feared judgment for being too celebratory.
The area may never be the same again, but Halloween 2026 seemed a step closer back to business as usual.
Halloween decorations were popping up through the neighborhood over the past few weeks, and hardcore Christians were out protesting the holiday and its perceived queerness. But it was not until Friday that the crowds really started showing up.
On Saturday, the main road through Itaewon was closed off to road traffic — a precautioun that should have been taken four years ago — handing the street over to tens of thousands of pedestrians celebrating the holiday. Making room in the streets helped significantly to reduce the pressure on the local alleys.
People in costumes were out in larger numbers than the last couple years. There were people in silly costumes, scary costumes, gory costumes, many which would have been considered inappropriate in the previous two years. Notably, parents with young children were out in the area early on.
According to Yonhap, more than 32,000 people had gathered in Itaewon as of 10 p.m., but the crowd grew larger more after that. At 11:47 p.m., Line 6 subway trains began skipping Itaewon Station. At 11:50 p.m., an emergency text message was sent out notifying people to avoid Itaewon's World Culture Food Street due to overcrowding.
The wounds of Halloween 2022 will never fully heal, but the community has shown that it is finally ready to keep on living.
